title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026: Hardware Moves, Funding Stalls

stats.label: U.S. fusion companies tracked
stats.detail: Most pursue tokamaks or stellarators; others use laser-based inertial confinement (Fusion Industry Association, 2026).

stats.label: Private fusion funding, 12 months
stats.detail: Record worldwide raise to July 2026; cumulative funding since 2021 reached $14.24 billion.

stats.label: ITER sector modules installed
stats.detail: Two-thirds of the tokamak core is in the pit, almost six months ahead of schedule.

stats.label: U.S. target for fusion deployment
stats.detail: DOE's Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap, released in June, is the central plank of the strategy.

stats.label: Fusion science appropriation
stats.detail: Below the $805.7 million enacted, against up to $1.1 billion authorised for FY2027.

quotes.text: "The plan isn't the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding. If we underfund the U.S. fusion program and we cut vital scope, we can all watch the timeline to commercialisation slip."
quotes.source: Robb Hughes, Realta Fusion, via Reuters

quotes.text: "With six modules now in place, we are demonstrating that this technical approach is delivering tangible results on the project's critical path."
Private developers have not yet achieved "net energy gain" — the point where a fusion reaction produces more energy than was used to start and sustain it.
quotes.source: Reuters, US roadmap targets fusion deployment by mid 2030s

quotes.text: As of 2025, the National Ignition Facility is the only laboratory to have demonstrated a fusion energy gain factor above one; efficiencies orders of magnitude higher are needed for engineering breakeven.

takeaway: Fusion's 2026 story is hard hardware on schedule and private capital at record highs, but the commercial timeline still hinges on federal funding that came in under the enacted level.
